newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-FRENCH PENPIX FOR TOURNOI DE FRANCE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FRENCH PENPIX FOR TOURNOI DE FRANCE.

text.p: Profiles of French squad for the Tournoi de France starting on Tuesday:
Goalkeepers:

Fabien Barthez (Monaco), age 25, 3 caps. Has snatched place from Bernard Lama of Paris St Germain, first choice in Euro 96 last year, on basis of improved aerial play and greater command of whole penalty area, added to Lama's loss of form after early season injury.

Lionel Charbonnier (Auxerre) 30, 0. Won late call to national team after helping Auxerre reach European Cup quarter-finals this season. Sound in most aspects of goalkeeping and agile on line. Picked in place of Lama who was recently suspended for two months for using cannabis.
Defenders:

Laurent Blanc (Barcelona) 31, 59. Key figure in coach Aime Jacquet's World Cup plans, who rates higher currently at international than club level with Barcelona in Spanish league. With 11 goals for France has averaged one goal in six games, likes to break fast on attacking runs down middle.

Marcel Desailly (AC Milan) 28, 33. Plays in midfield ball-winning role for Italian club, starring in their spectacular 1994 European Cup victory over Barcelona, but forms solid and effective defensive partnership with Blanc.

Bruno N'Gotty (Paris St Germain) 25, 4. Reserve for Blanc or Desailly who can also fill defensive midfield role if needed. Will turn 26 on June 10, eve of France's closing match against Italy at his club's Parc des Princes ground.

Franck Leboeuf (Chelsea), 29, 9. Shaven-headed player who has enhanced international chances with good performances in first season with Chelsea ending with English F.A. Cup triumph. Has scored twice for his country.

Lilian Thuram (Parma) 25, 22. Has won place from veteran Jocelyn Angloma since Euro'96, gaining in experience since moving to the Italian league this season where he has been considered one of best defenders in serie A.
Vicent Candela (AS Roma) 23, 4. Sound defender also good coming forward who joined Roma from Guingamp at halfway break in French league season in December.

Bixente Lizarazu (Athletic Bilbao) 27, 27. Remains a Jacquet favourite despite injury-plagued season during which has missed several internationals. Better coming forward to join attack than defending.
Midfielders:

Didier Deschamps (Juventus) 28, 58. Made debut for France in 1989, captain and seemingly irreplaceable, missing only defeat of Jacquet's reign in Copenhagen in November. Unlucky not to win third European Cup winners medal last week after helping Marseille to crown in 1993 and Juventus in 1996.

Christian Karembeu (Sampdoria) 26, 26. Powerful New Caledonia-born ball-winning midfielder involved in tug-of-war between Real Madrid in mid-season, but appears set to see out contract in Italy until end of 1998 World Cup season.

Patrick Vieira (Arsenal) 20, 1. Promoted from under-21 side this year, has matured at the north London club with regular performances under Arsene Wenger after seldom getting a game at star-studded AC Milan. Good at winning ball deep in midfield and carrying it into opposition territory.
Pierre Laigle (Sampdoria) 26, 5. Has everything still to prove in French colours. Defensive midfielder who likes to carry ball down flanks.

Zinedine Zidane (Juventus) 24, 23. Nearest thing yet to a true successor to Michel Platini at Juventus. Failed to crown an otherwise remarkable first season in tough serie A by ending on losing side in European Cup final last week. Has won world club title, European Super Cup and Italian title since December.
Forwards:
Ibrahim Ba (Bordeaux) 24, 3. Gifted and physically powerful runner who generally plays on right and made big impact on international debut scoring in 2-0 away win over Portugal in January.

Youri Djorkaeff (Inter Milan) 29, 27. Has enhanced reputation in first season in Italy becoming one of Inter's top players, although disappointed to end season without trophy after UEFA Cup final defeat. Striker and midfielder combined, scoring or making goals. Has scored 14 times for France.

Patrice Loko (Paris St Germain) 27, 25. Hard working forward who has low scoring rate for France (seven goals) but creates space for others. Scored 15 league goals for PSG this season, including four in one match against Nice, and hat-trick in second leg of European Cup Winners' Cup quarter-final away to AEK Athens.

Christophe Dugarry (AC Milan) 25, 18. Like Loko, has low scoring rate (two goals) for striker at international level, preferring to make rather than take chances. Lucky to retain place in Jacquet's squad given few chances for first team football at Milan.

Florian Maurice (Lyon) 23, 1. Would have been a regular for France all season had be not ruptured his Achilles tendon three days after his August debut against Mexico. Fast, skilled striker who Jacquet hopes will solve goal scoring deficit.

Nicolas Ouedec (Espanyol) 25, 6. Unlucky not to add to his caps total this season because of injuries, missing all France's games after scoring against Mexico in August. Has new chance to prove he could renew effective partnership with Loko that helped brilliant young Nantes side win 1995 French championship.
Marc Keller (Karlsruhe) 29, 3. Cunning striker who was one of leading scorers in French first division with Strasbourg two years ago. Has university degree in economics.

Robert Pires (Metz) 24, 5. Busy winger who roams across front of attack and also drops into deep positions to help build attacks. Has scored twice already in short France career, including winner against the Netherlands in February.
